verdicts.title: Meta-Mathematics of Computational Complexity Theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We survey results on the formalization and independence of mathematical statements related to major open problems in computational complexity theory. Our primary focus is on recent findings concerning the (un)provability of complexity bounds within theories of bounded arithmetic. This includes the techniques employed and related open problems, such as the (non)existence of a feasible proof that P = NP.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract is a survey of bounded arithmetic formalization and independence results around complexity open problems ('formalization and independence of mathematical statements related to major open problems'), with no mention of groupoid representation dimensions or Frege proof depth bounds on CNF formulas.

verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory, matrix powering, and orbit closures in algebraic complexity—'no orbit occurrence obstructions that prove even superlinear lower bounds'—with no mention of groupoid representation dimension, CNF formulas, or Frege proof depth.

verdicts.title: The groupoid structure of groupoid morphisms
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper we construct two groupoids from morphisms of groupoids, with one from a categorical viewpoint and the other from a geometric viewpoint. We show that for each pair of groupoids, the two kinds of groupoids of morphisms are equivalent. Then we study the automorphism groupoid of a groupoid.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns constructing groupoids of morphisms between groupoids and studying automorphism groupoids — purely category-theoretic structure. It makes no mention of CNF formulas, Frege proof depth, representation dimension bounds, or proof complexity.
